BURHAN:v3p85/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p85/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p85/r8.claim: Some treat the lām in لك as strengthening, while others attach it to an implicit predicate describing the enemy as specifically yours.
BURHAN:v3p85/r8.anchor: وقيل بل يتعلق بمستقر محذوف صفة لعدو وهي للاختصاص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p389/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p389/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p389/r9.claim: The prohibition against being expelled means Adam and Eve must not obey Satan’s temptation; Satan is credited with the expulsion because his whispering caused their act, though God effected it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p389/r9.anchor: وأسند الإخراج إليه وإن كان المخرج هو الله تعالى لما كان بوسوسته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p389/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p389/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p389/r10.claim: The verb meaning you will suffer may be subjunctive after the prohibition or indicative as a separate prediction; it is singular because Adam is addressed and his household’s hardship follows his.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p389/r10.anchor: فتشقى يحتمل أن يكون منصوبا بإضمار أن في جواب النهي، وأن يكون مرفوعا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p390/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p390/r1.speaker: قول أول
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p390/r1.claim: Suffering may mean the toil of earning food, which primarily falls on the man.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p390/r1.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالشقاء التعب في طلب القوت وذلك راجع إلى الرجل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p390/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p390/r2.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p390/r2.claim: Ibn Jubayr reports that Adam was given a red ox to plow, so he ate by the labor and sweat of his hand.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p390/r2.anchor: وعن ابن جبير: أهبط له ثور أحمر يحرث عليه فيأكل بكد يمينه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p76/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p76/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p76/r2.claim: Satan’s jealous refusal of prostration became a challenge to God: he claimed humans were unworthy of superiority and Paradise and that most would follow him; God granted respite while warning him and his followers of Hell. The passage warns Adam that Satan is the enemy who may drive him and his wife from Paradise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p76/r2.anchor: Not only did Satan refuse prostration

SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r1.claim: فتشقى is subjunctive with an implied أن in the response to the prohibition.
SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r1.anchor: قوله: { فتشقى }: منصوب بإضمار " أن " في جواب النهي.

SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r2.claim: Although the prohibition is addressed on its surface to Iblis, it is intended for Adam and his wife: they must not pursue expulsion, which would bring worldly toil and hardship.
SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r2.anchor: أي: لا تتعاطيا أسباب الخروج فيحصل لكما الشقاء

SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r3.claim: The hardship meant here is specifically worldly effort and toil.
SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r3.anchor: فيحصل لكما الشقاء، وهو الكد والتعب الدنيوي خاصة.

SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r4.claim: The Shaykh proposes an indicative reading as a new sentence, meaning you will then suffer; the author considers this remote or impossible because the point is not merely to predict Adam's suffering.
SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مرفوعا على الاستئناف أي: فأنت تشقى. كذا قدره الشيخ.

SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r5.claim: The singular suffering is assigned to Adam because men head family affairs, and the verse ending makes the wording apt.
SAMIN-DURR:20:117/r5.anchor: وأسند الشقاوة إليه دونها؛ لأن الأمور معصوبة برؤوس الرجال. وحسن ذلك

ASAD-NOTES:20:115#n102/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:115#n102/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:115#n102/r1.claim: The commandment, more precisely a warning, is stated in 20:117.
ASAD-NOTES:20:115#n102/r1.anchor: The relevant divine commandment - or, rather, warning - is spelled out in verse 117.

ASAD-NOTES:20:116/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:116/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:116/r2.claim: God warns Adam and his wife that their foe could drive them from the garden and make Adam unhappy.
ASAD-NOTES:20:116/r2.anchor: Verily, this is a foe unto thee and thy wife: so let him not drive the two of you out of this garden and render thee unhappy.

ASAD-NOTES:20:116#n104/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:116#n104/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:116#n104/r1.claim: Asad takes the wording literally as “so that thou wilt become unhappy” and refers readers to his note on the garden in surah 2.
ASAD-NOTES:20:116#n104/r1.anchor: Lit., "so that thou wilt become unhappy". Regarding the significance of "the garden" spoken of here

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p229/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p229/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p229/r4.claim: The Quran uses zauj for Adam's spouse, including in 2:35, 7:19, and 20:117.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p229/r4.anchor: البيان القرآني يستعمل لفظ "زوج" حيثما تحدث عن آدم وزوجه: (آيات البقرة 35 والأعراف 19 وطه 117)

ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r1.claim: God spoke after the preceding events out of concern to counsel Adam.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r1.anchor: عقيب ذلك اعتناء بنصح إدم عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r2.claim: The preposition is repeated because, according to most grammarians, a preposition cannot coordinate directly onto a genitive pronoun without repetition.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r2.anchor: لأنه لايعطف على الضمير المجرور بدون إعادة الجار عند الجمهور

ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r3.claim: Some say the repeated lām stresses that Satan is intrinsically Eve’s enemy, not merely so through his enmity to Adam.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r3.anchor: للدلالة على أن عداوة اللعين للزوجة اصالة لاتبعا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r4.claim: Even if repeating the preposition is grammatically obligatory, that does not prevent it from serving the contextual emphasis proposed by Ibn Malik’s position.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r4.anchor: كون الشئ لازما بحسب القاعدة النحوية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r5.claim: Calling her Adam’s wife rather than naming Hawwa adds aversion to Satan and strengthens the warning.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r5.anchor: في التعبير بزوجك دون حواء من مزيد التنفير والتحذير

ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r6.claim: One explanation is that Satan’s enmity arose simply from envy; Satan and his followers were the first to envy.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r6.anchor: فقيل مجرد الحسد وهو لعنه الله تعالى ولعن اتباعه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r7.claim: Another explanation contrasts the old, ignorant Satan with the young, learned Adam; the ignorant are characteristically enemies of the learned.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r7.anchor: كونه شيخا جاهلا وكون آدم عليه السلام شابا عالما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r8.claim: A third explanation is the opposition of their origins: Satan was created from fire, Adam from clay, and Hawwa from Adam.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r8.anchor: فإن اللعين خلق من نار وآدم عليه السلام خلق من طين وحواء خلقت منه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r9.claim: The prohibition means they must not let Satan become the cause of their expulsion; it indirectly forbids placing themselves where he can expel them.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r9.anchor: فلا يكونن سببا لأخراجكما ( من الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r10.claim: The indirect prohibition is comparable to the address “let there be no constriction in your breast” in 7:2.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r11.claim: The fāʾ orders the prohibition as a consequence of Satan’s enmity, or of being informed about that enmity.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r11.anchor: والفاء لترتيب موجب النهي على عداوته لهما أو على الأخبار بها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r12.claim: The hardship is the multitude of worldly travails, from which no one is spared; Adam alone is named because he is primary in household affairs and his toil entails his wife’s, while the wording also completes the cadence.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r12.anchor: وإسناد ذلك إليه عليه السلام خاصة بعد تعليق الإخراج الموجب له بهما معا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r13.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r13.claim: Some restrict the hardship to earning the means of livelihood, which they regard as men’s responsibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r13.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالشقاء التعب في تحصيل مبادى المعاش

ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r14.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r14.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports that after Adam was sent down he was told to work a piebald ox; wiping sweat, Adam recognized this as the promised toil, then blamed Hawwa. Transmitted by ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn ʿAsakir, and others; no grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r14.anchor: عن سعيد ابن جبير قال : إن آدم عليه السلام لما اهبط من الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r15.claim: Although the livelihood reading has supporting material, al-Alusi finds it debatable and prefers the broader meaning of hardship.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r15.anchor: وكذا أيد بالآية بعد وفيه تأمل ولعل القول بالعموم أولى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r16.claim: The verb may be subjunctive with an understood an after the prohibition, or indicative as a new clause meaning “then you will suffer”; al-Alusi rejects the latter because the point is a consequence, not a prediction.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r16.anchor: تشقى ) يحتمل أن يكون منصوبا بإضمار أن في جواب النهي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r2.claim: Adam’s wife in this address is Eve.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r2.anchor: إن هذا عدو لك ولزوجك} حواء،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r3.claim: Adam would be wearied and toil, earning his livelihood through labor and sweat.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r3.anchor: يعني: تتعب وتنصب، ويكون عيشك من كد يمينك بعرق جبينك.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r4.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r4.claim: Al-Suddī identifies Adam’s toil as plowing, planting, harvesting, grinding, and baking.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r4.anchor: قال السدي: يعني الحرث والزرع والحصيد والطحن والخبيز.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r5.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reports that a red bull was sent down to Adam; he plowed with it and wiped sweat from his brow, which was his hardship.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r5.anchor: وعن سعيد 14/ب بن جبير: قال أهبط إلى آدم ثور أحمر، فكان يحرث عليه، ويمسح العرق عن جبينه، فذلك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r6.claim: The singular returns the hardship to Adam rather than saying both spouses toil, since his burden is greater and the man works to support his wife.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r6.anchor: ولم يقل: "فتشقيا" رجوعا به إلى آدم، لأن تعبه أكثر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p298/r7.claim: Another explanation for the singular wording is that it preserves the verse endings.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:117/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:117/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:117/r1.claim: The warning means do not become a cause through which Satan brings about your expulsion.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:117/r1.anchor: فلا يكونن سببا لإخراجكما، والمراد نهيهما عن أن يكون

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:117/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:117/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:117/r2.claim: Although both are expelled, hardship is assigned to Adam because his suffering entails hers as provider, and for the verse's cadence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:117/r2.anchor: وأفرده بإسناد الشقاء إليه بعد إشراكهما في الخروج اكتفاء باستلزام شقائه شقاءها

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:117/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:117/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:117/r3.claim: Alternatively hardship means toil to earn a living, traditionally the man's task; the following verses support this reading.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:117/r3.anchor: أو لأن المراد بالشقاء التعب في طلب المعاش وذلك وظيفة الرجال ويؤيده قوله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r1.claim: The sūra's purpose is to show God's forbearance toward those who stray and His power over rejecters; Adam's failure is first summarized and then detailed, naming it disobedience to warn against forbidden acts and direct the deficient toward prompt repentance.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r1.anchor: ذكر فعله آدم عليه السلام هذه في هذه السورة بلفظ المعصية مع التصريح بأنها وجه النسيان , وذكر ذلك أولا مجملا ثم أتبعه تفصيله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r6.claim: The warning is directed to Satan while its intended protection is for Adam and his wife; it spares her a direct prohibition, and assigning the expulsion to Satan intensifies the warning.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r6.anchor: وجه النهي إليه والمراد : هما , تنبيها على أن لها من الجلالة ما ينبغي أن تصان عن أن يتوجه إليها نهي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r7.claim: God warns that Satan will persist in seeking their harm and removal from the Garden.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r7.anchor: فإنه لا يقصر في ضركما وإرادة إنزالكما عنها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r8.claim: Although Eve shares the expulsion and its effects, the verse singles out Adam's toil because the author sees the man as responsible for labor, protection, and care, especially for his wife; an upright husband guides her to good, while a corrupt one leads her to harm.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r8.anchor: وكان أغلب تعبه في أمر المرأة , أفرد لاتحذير منه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p52/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p52/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p52/r1.claim: Here misery means worldly toil from expulsion, not ultimate misery: if that were intended, Adam could not later have entered the Garden, and the clause after fa is a predicate that cannot fail.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p52/r1.anchor: لأنه لو أرادها ما دخل الجنة بعد ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p52/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p52/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p52/r2.claim: Exile would remove the four supports of human sufficiency: satiety, drink, clothing, and shelter.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p52/r2.anchor: من الأقطاب التي يدور علها كفاف الإنسان , وهي الشبع والري والكسوة والكن

BIQAI-FULL:v5p52/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p52/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p52/r3.claim: The verse names the opposites of these blessings by negation so Adam hears the kinds of misery he was warned against and recoils from their cause, while learning that caution cannot defeat destiny.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p52/r3.anchor: بافظ النفي لنقائضها ليطرق سمعه بأسماء أصناف الشقوة

DURR-FULL:v5p605/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r1.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r1.claim: Sufyan notes that the verse uses the singular rather than the dual فتشقيان; Eve entered with Adam, so its singular masculine address includes her.
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r1.anchor: عن سفيان بن عينية قال: لم يقل فتشقيان لأنها دخلت معه فوقع المعنى عليهما جميعا

DURR-FULL:v5p605/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r2.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r2.claim: Sufyan extends the meaning to their descendants and compares the singular address to 65:1 and 66:1, which address the Prophet while including others.
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r2.anchor: عن سفيان بن عينية قال: لم يقل فتشقيان لأنها دخلت معه فوقع المعنى عليهما جميعا وعلى أولادهما كقوله: (يا أيها النبي إذا طلقتم)

DURR-FULL:v5p605/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r3.claim: Said ibn Jubayr reports that Adam, made to work an ox after descending, wiped sweat from his brow and recognized the toil as what God had warned of; he blamed Eve, and descendants repeated that blame when working oxen.
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنهما قال: إن آدم عليه السلام لما أهبط إلى الأرض استقبله ثور أبلق فقيل له: اعمل عليه فجعل يمسح العرق عن جبينه

BURSEVI:v5p334/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p334/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p334/r1.claim: The Persian couplet contrasts one who sees only Adam’s body and recoils with one who sees the entrusted divine light and bows.
BURSEVI:v5p334/r1.anchor: آنكه آدم را بدن ديد اورميد وانكه نور مؤتمن ديد او خميد

BURSEVI:v5p334/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p334/r2.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v5p334/r2.claim: Iblis may derive from ablasa, to despair and become bewildered, or may be a foreign word, as al-Qamus says.
BURSEVI:v5p334/r2.anchor: يقال أبلس يئس وتحير ومنه إبليس أو هو أعجمي كما في "القاموس"

BURSEVI:v5p334/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p334/r3.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v5p334/r3.claim: Al-Mufradat defines ibaʾ as especially strong refusal: every act of ibaʾ is refusal, but not every refusal is ibaʾ.
BURSEVI:v5p334/r3.anchor: قال في "المفردات" : الإباء شدة الامتناع فكل إباء امتناع وليس كل امتناع إباء

BURSEVI:v5p334/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p334/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p334/r4.claim: Immediately after Satan refused to bow, God addressed Adam to care for and warn him.

BURSEVI:v5p334/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p334/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p334/r5.claim: This contemptible figure refers to Satan, whose deed Adam had just witnessed; the wife is Eve.

BURSEVI:v5p334/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p334/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p334/r6.claim: Zawj means one member of a pair, male or female, on condition that another of the same kind accompanies it.
BURSEVI:v5p334/r6.anchor: والزوج اسم للفرد بشرط أن يكون معه آخر من جنسه ذكرا كان أو أنثى

BURSEVI:v5p334/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p334/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p334/r7.claim: Satan became Adam’s enemy through envy: when he saw God’s favors on Adam, he envied him and sought to ruin his condition.
BURSEVI:v5p334/r7.anchor: نعم الله على آدم حسده فصار عدوا له

BURSEVI:v5p334/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p334/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p334/r8.claim: The lesson is that an envier becomes an enemy who wants another’s destruction and works to corrupt his circumstances.
BURSEVI:v5p334/r8.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن كل من حسد أحدا يكون عدوا له ويريد هلاكه ويسعى في إفساد حاله

BURSEVI:v5p334/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p334/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p334/r9.claim: Another reason is that Adam was a young scholar whereas Iblis was an ignorant elder who judged merit by ancestry; the author generalizes that the ignorant are enemies of what they do not know.
BURSEVI:v5p334/r9.anchor: والثاني أنه كان شابا عالما وإبليس شيخا جاهلا لأنه أثبت فضيلته بفضيلة أصله

BURSEVI:v5p334/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p334/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p334/r10.claim: The accompanying Persian-Arabic line says a person remains an enemy of what he does not know.
BURSEVI:v5p334/r10.anchor: المرء لا يزال عدوا لما جهل

BURSEVI:v5p334/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p334/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p334/r11.claim: A third explanation is inherited hostility between their origins: Iblis was made of fire, while Adam was made of water and earth.
BURSEVI:v5p334/r11.anchor: والثالث أنه مخلوق من النار وآدم من الماء والتراب وبين أصليهما عداوة فبقيت العداوة فيهما

BURSEVI:v5p334/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p334/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p334/r12.claim: Satan is only the cause of their expulsion; the wording assigns the act to its cause, while God is the actual expeller.
BURSEVI:v5p334/r12.anchor: لا يكونن سببا لإخراجكما منها فهو من قبيل إسناد الفعل إلى السبب وإلا فالمخرج حقيقة هو الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v5p334/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p334/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p334/r13.claim: Although phrased as a prohibition to Satan, the intended argument is that Adam and Eve must not put themselves in a position where Satan can cause their expulsion.
BURSEVI:v5p334/r13.anchor: وظاهره وإن كان نهي إبليس عن الإخراج إلا أن المراد نهيهما من أن يكونا بحيث يتسبب الشيطان في إخراجهما منها

BURSEVI:v5p334/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p334/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p334/r14.claim: The consequence of the prohibition uses a singular masculine form for Adam, both to preserve the verse endings and because the hardship principally falls on him.
BURSEVI:v5p334/r14.anchor: {فتشقى} جواب للنهي وإسناد الشقاء إليه لرعاية الفواصل ولأصالته

BURSEVI:v5p334/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p334/r15.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v5p334/r15.claim: Al-Raghib contrasts hardship with happiness and says both worldly and afterlife hardship have categories; worldly hardship, like happiness, may be personal, bodily, or external.
BURSEVI:v5p334/r15.anchor: قال في المفردات الشقاوة خلاف السعادة وكما أن السعادة ضربان سعادة دنيوية وسعادة أخروية ثم السعادة الدنيوية ثلاثة أضرب

BURSEVI:v5p334/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p334/r16.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v5p334/r16.claim: Al-Raghib links worldly hardship here with hardship in the afterlife described for the one who rejects guidance.
BURSEVI:v5p334/r16.anchor: وفي الشقاوة الأخروية قال تعالى : {فمن اتبع هداى فلا يضل ولا يشقى} وفي الدنيوية {فلا يخرجنكما من الجنة فتشقى}

BURSEVI:v5p334/r17.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p334/r17.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v5p334/r17.claim: Al-Qamus also gives shaqā the sense of hardship and difficulty, with a long final vowel.
BURSEVI:v5p334/r17.anchor: كما قال في "القاموس" الشقا الشدة والعسر ويمد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r1.claim: Adam’s creation and the angels’ prostration were already related in al-Baqara and al-Aʿraf; Ibn ʿĀshūr focuses here on what is distinctive in this sura’s wording.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r1.anchor: قصة خلق آدم وسجود الملائكة له وإباء الشيطان من السجود تقدمت في سورة البقرة وسورة الأعراف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r2.claim: إن هذا points contemptuously to Satan; the author compares it with the pagans’ dismissive question about the man criticizing their gods.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r2.anchor: فقوله { إن هذا } إشارة إلى الشيطان إشارة مرادا منها التحقير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r3.claim: This verse refers to the adversary by a demonstrative, whereas al-Aʿraf names Satan directly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r3.anchor: وفي سورة الأعراف ( 22 ) إن الشيطان لكما عدو عبر عنه باسمه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r4.claim: Unlike the general statement in al-Aʿraf, this verse details the targets of Satan’s hostility, naming Adam first as its original object and Eve as its extension through her relation to him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r4.anchor: فذكرت عداوته لهما جملة هنالك وذكرت تفصيلا هنا ، فابتدىء في ذكر متعلق عداوته بآدم لأن آدم هو منشأ عداوة الشيطان لحسده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r5.claim: Satan envies both because God gave them knowledge of names, the basis of thought leading to guidance and speech that enables instruction; this frustrates his seduction of them and their descendants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r5.anchor: وهي حسده إياهما على ما وهبهما الله من علم الأسماء الذي هو عنوان الفكر الموصل إلى الهدى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r6.claim: Satan believed himself more deserving of honor than Adam and became resentful when ordered to prostrate to him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r6.anchor: ولأن الشيطان رأى نفسه أجدر بالتفضيل على آدم فحنق لما أمر بالسجود لآدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r7.claim: The warning follows from Satan’s hostility: an enemy does not want his opponent’s well-being, so Adam and Eve must beware of being expelled.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r7.anchor: تفريع على الإخبار بعداوة إبليس له ولزوجه : بأن نهيا نهي تحذير عن أن يتسبب إبليس في خروجهما من الجنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r8.claim: The prohibition is phrased as Satan’s act, a pointed indirect way of telling Adam not to be swayed by means of expulsion; it does not mean merely that he must prevent news of his act reaching God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r8.anchor: ووقع النهي في صورة نهي عن عمل هو من أعمال الشيطان لا من أعمال آدم كناية عن نهي آدم عن التأثر بوسائل إخراجهما من الجنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r1.claim: Hardship is attributed to Adam alone for concision: one spouse’s suffering affects the other, and the wording hints that the man’s hardship is the woman’s starting point while preserving the verse ending.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r1.anchor: وأسند ترتب الشقاء إلى آدم خاصة دون زوجه إيجازا ، لأن في شقاء أحد الزوجين شقاء الآخر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67/r1.claim: Adam and Eve must not obey Satan's seduction, which would cause their expulsion from Paradise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67/r1.anchor: أي لا يقع منكما طاعة له في إغوائه فيكون ذلك سبب خروجكما من الجنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67/r2.claim: The singular address focuses on Adam as the initial addressee and intended subject.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67/r2.anchor: ثم خصص بقوله فتشقى من حيث كان المخاطب أولا والمقصود في الكلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67/r3.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67/r3.claim: Another explanation says hardship in worldly livelihood is assigned to men, explaining the singular address.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67/r3.anchor: وقيل بل ذلك لأن الله تعالى جعل الشقاء في معيشة الدنيا في حيز الرجال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67/r4.claim: A report says Adam descended with a red ox, plowed with it, and wiped sweat away; this was the hardship warned of.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67/r4.anchor: وروي أن آدم لما أهبط هبط معه ثور أحمر فكأن يحرث ويمسح العرق فهذا هو الشقاء الذي خوف منه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p328/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p328/r1.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p328/r1.claim: The exegetes understand Adam's suffering as the toil of earthly life: plowing, farming, kneading, baking, and similar labor.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p328/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون المراد به نصب الدنيا وتعبها من تكلف الحرث والزرع والعجن والخبز وغير ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p328/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p328/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p328/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says Adam was sent down with a red ox to work, wiping sweat from his brow; that was his hardship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p328/r2.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير أهبط إلى آدم ثور أحمر فكان يعتمل عليه ويمسح العرق عن جبينه فذلك شقاؤه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p328/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p328/r3.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p328/r3.claim: Al-Farra explains the singular address as sufficient for Adam and Eve together, citing the singular “sitter” on the right and left.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p328/r3.anchor: أحدهما أن آدم هو المخاطب فاكتفى به مثله عن اليمين وعن الشمال قعيد ق 17 قاله الفراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p328/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p328/r4.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p328/r4.claim: Al-Mawardi says Adam is singled out because he was the provider and bore the greater share of the toil.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p328/r4.anchor: والثاني أنه لما كان آدم هو الكاسب كان التعب في حقه أكثر ذكره الماوردي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p320/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p320/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p320/r6.claim: The enemy addressed is Iblis, and Adam's wife is Hawwa.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p320/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p320/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p320/r7.claim: God warns Adam not to let Iblis strive to expel them from Paradise, where Adam enjoys ease, lest he toil and suffer seeking his livelihood.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p320/r7.anchor: أي: إياك أن يسعى (5) في إخراجك منها، فتتعب وتعنى وتشقى

JISHUMI:v7p4754/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r4.claim: The enemy warned about is Iblis, whose deception and whispering could expel Adam and his wife from the Garden.
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r4.anchor: يعني إبليس عدو لك ولزوجك حواء فلا يخرجنكما من الجنة بغرور هو وساوسه

JISHUMI:v7p4754/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r5.claim: One explanation says Adam’s toil is worldly hardship, earning his livelihood and necessities after expulsion.
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r5.anchor: قيل: هي شقاوة الدنيا وهو أن يأكل من كده وكسبه

JISHUMI:v7p4754/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r6.claim: The singular address means both spouses will toil because they share the same cause; other explanations invoke masculine grammatical dominance or the verse endings.
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r6.anchor: وإنما قال: فتشقى على خطاب الواحد والمعنى فتشقى أنت وزوجك؛ لأن أمرهما في السبب واحد

JISHUMI:v7p4754/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r7.claim: Another explanation says the singular is used because the husband is responsible for his wife’s maintenance and work.
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r7.anchor: وقيل: لأن نفقة المرأة على الزوج، فكان العمل عليه

JISHUMI:v7p4754/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r8.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says a red bull came down to Adam; Adam plowed with it and wiped sweat from his brow, exemplifying the toil.
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r8.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: هبط على آدم ثور أحمر، فكان يحرث عليه ويمسح العرق عن جبينه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p92/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p92/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p92/r1.claim: The warning means that Satan must not become the cause of their expulsion from the Garden.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p92/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p92/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p92/r2.claim: The singular hardship is assigned to Adam though both are expelled because the husband's hardship as household head includes his family, just as his happiness includes them; it also preserves the verse ending.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p92/r2.anchor: لأن في ضمن شقاء الرجل وهو قيم أهله وأميرهم شقاءهم ، كما أن في ضمن سعادته سعادتهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p92/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p92/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p92/r3.claim: Alternatively, hardship means toil in seeking sustenance, which falls primarily on the man and thus returns to Adam.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p92/r3.anchor: أو أريد بالشقاء التعب في طلب القوت ، وذلك معصوب برأس الرجل وهو راجع إليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p92/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p92/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p92/r4.claim: A report says Adam was sent down with a red ox, plowed with it, and wiped sweat from his brow.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p92/r4.anchor: وروي أنه أهبط إلى آدم ثور أحمر فكان يحرث عليه ويمسح العرق من جبينه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r8.claim: The hardship is attached to Adam although its cause applies equally to him and his wife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r8.anchor: يعني أنت وزوجك لأنهما في استواء العلة واحد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r9.claim: The singular “you will suffer” addresses Adam alone; he is directly addressed and bears the work and earning for his wife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r9.anchor: ولم يقل : فتشقيا لأمرين : أحدهما : لأنه المخاطب دونها . الثاني : لأنه الكاد والكاسب لها , فكان بالشقاء أخص

MUQATIL:20:115-118/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:115-118/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:115-118/r5.claim: God warned Adam and Eve that Satan would make Adam toil: before sin he ate freely without working, but afterward worked for his food.
MUQATIL:20:115-118/r5.anchor: كان يأكل من الجنة رغدا من غير أن يعمل بيده

NASAFI-FULL:v3p70/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70/r1.claim: Satan is Adam and his wife’s enemy because he did not prostrate and did not accept Adam.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p70/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70/r2.claim: The warning means Satan must not become the cause of their expulsion from the Garden.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p70/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70/r3.claim: The singular “you suffer” fits the verse endings; it may also make the wife implicit, since the man provides for her.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70/r3.anchor: ولم يعل فتشقيا سراعاه لرؤس الاى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p70/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70/r4.claim: The suffering is the toil of seeking the means to live.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p70/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70/r5.claim: A report says Adam was sent down with a red ox, plowed with it, and wiped sweat from his brow.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70/r5.anchor: وروى أنه اهبط إلى أدم ثور احمر وكان يحرث عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r2.claim: The prohibition means do not accept Satan's temptation, which would cause their expulsion.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r2.anchor: نهى ومجازه: لا تقبلا منه فيكون ذلك سببا لخروجكما

QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r3.claim: The singular hardship includes Adam and his wife because their cause is the same; Adam is grammatically addressed and intended.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r3.anchor: يعني أنت وزوجك لأنهما في استواء العلة واحد ولم يقل: فتشقيا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r4.claim: Adam is singled out because he bears the work and earning that makes hardship especially his.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r4.anchor: وأيضا لما كان الكاد عليها والكاسب لها كان بالشقاء أخص

QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r5.claim: Another view says both were expelled but bodily hardship is assigned only to Adam, as clarified by the following descriptions of garden life.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r5.anchor: وقيل: الإخراج واقع عليهما والشقاوة على آدم وحده، وهو شقاوة البدن

QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r7.claim: The singular wording teaches that a husband's maintenance is owed to his wife; the four necessities are food, drink, clothing, and housing.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r7.anchor: وإنما خصه بذكر الشقاء ولم يقل فتشقيان: يعلمنا أن نفقة الزوجة على الزوج

QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r9.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes Adam's hardship to mean worldly hardship, since no human lives without toil.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r9.anchor: قال الحسن المراد بقوله: «فتشقى» شقاء الدنيا لا يرى ابن آدم إلا ناصبا.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r10.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r10.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the hardship is having to eat from the work of one's own hands.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r10.anchor: وقال الفراء: هو أن يأكل من كد يديه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r11.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r11.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Adam was sent down a red ox to plow with and wipe sweat from his brow; this was his hardship.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r11.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: أهبط إلى آدم ثور أحمر فكان يحرث عليه، ويمسح العرق عن جبينه،

QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r12.claim: A story says Gabriel gave Adam grain from Paradise; after planting, harvesting, processing, and baking it, Adam chased a rolling loaf and learned worldly provision would require toil.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r12.anchor: وقيل: لما أهبط من الجنة كان من أول شقائه أن جبريل أنزل عليه حبات من الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r8.claim: One explanation for Iblīs’s enmity is envy of the divine favors Adam received.
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r8.anchor: أن إبليس كان حسودا فلما رآى آثار نعم الله تعالى في حق آدم عليه السلام حسده فصار عدوا له

RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r9.claim: A second explanation contrasts the young, learned Adam, taught the names (2:31), with the old, ignorant Iblīs, whose claim of superiority by ancestry showed ignorance; an old ignorant person is an enemy to a young scholar.
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r9.anchor: أن آدم كان شابا عالما لقوله وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها ، وإبليس كان شيخا جاهلا

RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r10.claim: A third explanation says the enmity persisted because Iblīs was made from fire and Adam from water and earth, so their origins were opposed.
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r10.anchor: أن إبليس مخلوق من النار وآدم مخلوق من الماء والتراب فبين أصليهما عداوة

RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r1.claim: Although God is the one who expelled Adam and Eve, it is properly attributed to Satan because his seduction caused the act that led to their expulsion.
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r1.anchor: لما كان بوسوسته هو الذي فعل ما ترتب عليه الخروج صح ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r2.claim: Adam alone is named as suffering because the hardship of a household is included in that of its male head and ruler, while the phrasing also preserves the verse’s cadence.
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r2.anchor: أن في ضمن شقاء الرجل وهو قيم أهله وأميرهم شقاءهم كما أن في ضمن سعادته سعادتهم

RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r3.claim: A second explanation is that the suffering means the labor of seeking food, which falls on the man rather than the woman.
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r3.anchor: أريد بالشقاء التعب في طلب القوت وذلك على الرجل دون المرأة

RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r4.claim: An account says a red bull was sent down to Adam; he plowed with it and wiped sweat from his brow.
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r4.anchor: وروي أنه أهبط إلى آدم ثور أحمر وكان يحرث عليه ويمسح العرق عن جبينه

RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r8.claim: Freedom from hunger, nakedness, thirst, and sun exposure explains the misery mentioned in the preceding warning.
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r8.anchor: تفسير الشقاء المذكور في قوله : { فتشقى }

QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r9.claim: God knew Adam and Eve would undergo hardship after leaving Paradise, although the verse singles out Adam as the one who would suffer.
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r9.anchor: علم أنهم سيلقون ذلك الشقاء ؛ وأما إنه أضاف الشقاء إلى آدم وحده - وكلاهما لحقه شقاء الدنيا

QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r10.claim: One explanation for naming Adam alone is conformity to the surrounding verse endings.

QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r11.claim: Another explanation is that labor falls upon men rather than women.
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r11.anchor: أو لأن التعب على الرجال دون النساء

QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r12.claim: One who listens to an enemy will taste regret, too late for it to help.
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r12.anchor: ومن أصغى إلى قول عدوه فإنه يتجرع الندم ثم لا ينفعه

QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r13.claim: Adam's faith, God's warning, and Adam's certainty were unsurpassed, yet hardship made him regret and weep after the decree was settled.
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r13.anchor: ولا وعظ أشد رحمة من الله ، ولا يقين أقوى من يقينه . . . ولكن ما قاسى آدم الشقاء قبل ذلك

QUSHAYRI:v2p278/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p278/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p278/r3.claim: Although God knew Satan would whisper, Adam did not recall at the time that God had identified Satan as his enemy.
QUSHAYRI:v2p278/r3.anchor: وسوس إليه الشيطان وكان الحق يعلم ذلك ولم يذكر آدم في الحال أن هذا من نزعات من قال له - سبحانه - : { إن هذا عدو لك }

STUDYQURAN:20:117/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:117/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:117/r1.claim: The commentary links God's warning to Adam and Eve that Satan is their enemy to another account.
STUDYQURAN:20:117/r1.anchor: For the warning to Adam and Eve that Satan is an enemy unto them, see 7:21–22c

STUDYQURAN:20:117/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:117/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:117/r2.claim: The warning means Adam and Eve must not obey Satan, who would deceive them into eating from the forbidden tree and drive them from the Garden.
STUDYQURAN:20:117/r2.anchor: Let him not expel the two of you from the Garden is an admonition from God to Adam and Eve that they should not obey Satan

STUDYQURAN:20:117/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:117/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:117/r3.claim: “Wretched” refers to the hardship and fatigue of earning a livelihood in the world after leaving the Garden's comfort.
STUDYQURAN:20:117/r3.anchor: Such that thou wouldst be wretched refers to the hardship and fatigue that Adam and Eve would experience because of the need to earn a livelihood in this world

STUDYQURAN:20:117/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:117/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:117/r5.claim: The commentary points to other accounts of the warning, Satan's deception, the fall, and Adam and Eve's remorse.
STUDYQURAN:20:117/r5.anchor: For other accounts of Adam and Eve’s being warned by God, Satan’s deceiving them, their fall from Paradise, and their remorse over their actions

TAB-FULL:v16p186/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p186/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p186/r1.claim: God's reminder to Muhammad about Adam's lapse teaches that Adam's descendants will generally follow his path, except those God protects.
TAB-FULL:v16p186/r1.anchor: يكونوا في ذلك على منهاجه، إلا من عصمه الله منهم

TAB-FULL:v16p186/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p186/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p186/r2.claim: Satan's enmity is shown by his refusal to prostrate to Adam and his disobedience; the two must not obey him.
TAB-FULL:v16p186/r2.anchor: ولذلك من شنآنه لم يسجد لك، وخالف أمري في ذلك وعصاني، فلا تطيعاه فيما يأمركما به

TAB-FULL:v16p186/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p186/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p186/r3.claim: If Satan expels them through their disobedience and obedience to him, Adam's life will become toil earned by his own hands; this is the warned hardship.
TAB-FULL:v16p186/r3.anchor: فيخرجكما بمعصيتكما ربكما، وطاعتكما له {من الجنة فتشقى} [طه: 117] يقول: فيكون عيشك من كد يدك

TAB-FULL:v16p186/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p186/r4.speaker: سعيد
TAB-FULL:v16p186/r4.claim: Saʿid reports that Adam was given a red ox, plowed with it, and wiped sweat from his brow, exemplifying his toil after leaving the Garden.
TAB-FULL:v16p186/r4.anchor: عن جعفر، عن سعيد، قال: أهبط إلى آدم ثور أحمر، فكان يحرث عليه، ويمسح العرق من جبينه

TAB-FULL:v16p186/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p186/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p186/r5.claim: Though the warning addresses both Adam and his wife in the dual, the consequence is singular because the address began with Adam and stating his punishment sufficed.
TAB-FULL:v16p186/r5.anchor: وقال تعالى ذكره: {فتشقى} [طه: 117] ولم يقل: فتشقيا

TAB-FULL:v16p186/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p186/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p186/r6.claim: Al-Tabari compares the omitted companion in this singular construction to the singular wording about the two recording angels in Qaf 50:17.
TAB-FULL:v16p186/r6.anchor: كما قال: {عن اليمين وعن الشمال قعيد} [ق: 17] اجتزئ بمعرفة السامعين معناه

SULAMI:v1p451#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p451#2/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p451#2/r1.claim: Al-Wasiti says Adam concealed his enemy's hostility and did not implore God for protection, so he listened to the enemy's speech and oath.
SULAMI:v1p451#2/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : أضمر عداوته

SULAMI:v1p451#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p451#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p451#2/r2.claim: Ibn Ata explains the singular 'you will suffer' rather than dual 'you two will suffer': Adam knew the special rank of direct address while Eve did not, so he is named as the principal and she follows him.
SULAMI:v1p451#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء في هذه الآية : ﴿ فلا يخرجنكما من الجنة فتشقى ﴾

TABATABAI:20:116-117/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:116-117/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:116-117/r5.claim: God’s warning follows Iblis’s refusal to bow and counsels Adam for his own good; “this enemy” refers to Iblis.
TABATABAI:20:116-117/r5.anchor: تفريع على إباء إبليس عن السجدة أي فلما أبى قلنا إرشادا لآدم إلى ما فيه صلاح أمره ونصحا إن هذا الأبي

TABATABAI:20:116-117/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:116-117/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:116-117/r6.claim: The command not to let Iblis expel them indirectly means not to obey him or become careless about his scheme, lest he gain power to expel and make them suffer.
TABATABAI:20:116-117/r6.anchor: توجيه نهي إبليس عن إخراجهما من الجنة إلى آدم كناية عن نهيه عن طاعته أو عن الغفلة عن كيده

TABATABAI:20:116-117/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:116-117/r7.speaker: الرازي
TABATABAI:20:116-117/r7.claim: Al-Razi gives several explanations for Satan’s enmity, but al-Tabataba'i dismisses them as specious and not worth recounting.
TABATABAI:20:116-117/r7.anchor: وقد ذكر الإمام الرازي في تفسيره وجوها لسبب عداوة إبليس لآدم وزوجه وهي وجوه سخيفة

TABATABAI:20:116-117/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:116-117/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:116-117/r8.claim: The true reason for Satan’s enmity is his expulsion from divine proximity, his banishment, and the curse laid on him until resurrection, as his own words show.
TABATABAI:20:116-117/r8.anchor: والحق أن السبب فيها هو طرده من حضرة القرب ورجمه وجعل اللعن عليه إلى يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:20:117-122/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r1.claim: The honor given to Adam is honor for humankind as a species; the command to bow likewise concerned the human species, whose precedence over Satan led to Satan's expulsion and curse.
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r1.anchor: ومعلوم أن تكريم آدم عليه هو تكريم نوع الإنسان عليه كما أن أمره بالسجدة له

TABATABAI:20:117-122/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r2.claim: The hardship is toil: outside the garden, earthly life brings needs such as food, drink, clothing, and shelter, and effort to meet them; the next two verses explain the hardship.
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r2.anchor: والمراد بالشقاء التعب أي فتتعب إن خرجتما من الجنة وعشتما في غيرها وهو الأرض

TABATABAI:20:117-122/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r3.claim: The prohibition is advisory: disobeying brings the act's natural consequence, exhausting work for life's needs, not a sin that incurs afterlife punishment; it preceded religious legislation.
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r3.anchor: وهو أيضا دليل على أن النهي إرشادي ليس في مخالفته إلا الوقوع في المفسدة

TABATABAI:20:117-122/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r4.claim: The singular form addresses Adam because the covenant and speech were directed to him; the account uses singular forms for what concerns him and dual forms where both spouses must be included.
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r4.anchor: إن العهد إنما نزل على آدم عليه السلام وكان التكليم متوجها إليه

TABATABAI:20:117-122/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r5.claim: One explanation says the singular is used because the man supports his wife; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects this because the following verses also address Adam singularly, though the explanation would require dual forms.
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r5.anchor: من جهة أن نفقه المرأة على المرء ولذا نسب الشقاء وهو التعب

TABATABAI:20:117-122/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r6.claim: Another explanation attributes the singular to rhyme; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī dismisses this proposal.
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r6.anchor: وقيل إن الإفراد لرعاية الفواصل وهو كما ترى

TABRISI:20:124/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:124/r7.claim: The singular form means Adam would bear the toil of labor, earning, and supporting himself and his wife.
TABRISI:20:124/r7.anchor: أي فتقع في تعب العمل وكد الاكتساب والنفقة على زوجتك ونفسك ولذلك قال فتشقى ولم يقل فتشقيا

TABRISI:20:124/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124/r8.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:124/r8.claim: Another explanation is that both shared the same cause, so the wording treats them alike.
TABRISI:20:124/r8.anchor: وقيل: لأن أمرهما في السبب واحد فاستوى حكمهما لاستوائهما في السبب والعلة

TABRISI:20:124/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:124/r9.claim: A further explanation is that the singular wording keeps the verse endings aligned.

TABRISI:20:124/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:20:124/r10.claim: Sa‘id ibn Jubayr says Adam was given a red bull to plow with and sweated from his brow, which was the toil meant here.
TABRISI:20:124/r10.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: أنزل على آدم ثور أحمر فكان يحرث عليه ويرشح العرق عن جبينه

THALABI:v6p263/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p263/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p263/r10.claim: The enemy is Iblīs, and the wife addressed is Eve; expulsion would make Adam toil and earn his living through labor and sweat.
THALABI:v6p263/r10.anchor: فقلنا يا آدم إن هذا عدو لك ولزوجك حواء فلا يخرجنكما من الجنة فتتعب

THALABI:v6p263/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p263/r11.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v6p263/r11.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says a red bull was sent down to Adam to plow, and Adam wiped sweat from his brow; this was the hardship meant by the verse.
THALABI:v6p263/r11.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: أهبط إلى آدم ثور أحمر وكان يحرث عليه ويمسح العرق عن جبينه

THALABI:v6p263/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p263/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p263/r12.claim: Although the warning concerns both Adam and Eve, it uses the masculine singular because Adam's toil was greater; another explanation is the verse-end rhyme.
THALABI:v6p263/r12.anchor: وكان حقه أن يقول: فيشقيا ولكن غلب المذكر رجوعا به إلى آدم لأن تعبه أكثر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r1.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's report, Ibn ʿAbbās says the hardship is the toil and distress of worldly life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: (يريد شقاء الدنيا ونصبها)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r2.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan also understands worldly hardship, observing that Adam's descendants are all laboring and miserable.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن: (عني به شقاء الدنيا، ألا ترى ابن آدم إلا ناصبا شقيا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reports that Adam was sent down a red bull to work with, and had to wipe sweat from his brow; this was his hardship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r3.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: (أهبط إلى آدم ثورا أحمر كان يعتمل عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r4.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r4.claim: Al-Suddī specifies the labor as plowing, planting, kneading dough, and baking bread.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r5.speaker: زيد بن علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r5.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī glosses the hardship as the toil of earning a livelihood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r5.anchor: وقال زيد بن علي: (فتشقى في كد المعيشة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains the singular verb instead of a dual as addressing Adam, whose action stands for his wife's; singular address also suits the verse endings, like the singular sitter for the two sides in 50:17.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p544/r6.anchor: قال الفراء: (ولم يقل: فتشقيا، لأن آدم المخاطب وفي فعله اكتفاء من فعل المرأة)

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p283/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p283/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p283/r4.claim: If Adam and his wife disobey, God will expel them from Paradise and Adam will toil in this world.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p283/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p283/r5.speaker: بعضهم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p283/r5.claim: Some explain Adam’s hardship as having to eat from the work of his hands and the sweat of his brow.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p283/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم: تأكل من عمل يديك وعرق جبينك

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r2.claim: Earlier passages in Ṣād and al-Aʿrāf recount Adam, Iblis’s disobedience, the couple’s conditional stay in the garden, Satan’s enticement and their expulsion; retelling these matters in different contexts and styles is characteristic of the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r2.anchor: Yine A‘râf sûresinde Âdem’e –yasak ağaca yaklaşmamaları koşuluyla– eşiyle birlikte cennette kalma imkânı verildiğinden

BURHAN:v3p334/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p334/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p334/r3.claim: The Qur’an shifts from addressing two people to one, as when Pharaoh asks the pair who their Lord is but names Moses, and when Adam and Eve are told فتشقى.
BURHAN:v3p334/r3.anchor: الثالث من الاثنين إلى الواحد كقوله

BURHAN:v2p240/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p240/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
BURHAN:v2p240/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya explains the singular فتشقى as addressing Adam, the first person addressed and the main subject of the passage.
BURHAN:v2p240/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطية إنما أفرده بالشقاء من حيث كان المخاطب أولا

BURHAN:v2p240/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p240/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p240/r6.claim: Other explanations say worldly hardship is associated with men, or that the wording courteously leaves the woman unmentioned.
BURHAN:v2p240/r6.anchor: وقيل بل ذلك لأن الله جعل الشقاء في معيشة الدنيا في حيز الرجال

ITQAN:v3p90/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p90/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ITQAN:v3p90/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya explains the singular ‘you will suffer’ as directed to Adam because he was addressed first and was the main subject.
ITQAN:v3p90/r6.anchor: قال ابن عطية أفرده بالشقاء لأنه المخاطب أولا والمقصود في الكلام

ITQAN:v3p90/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p90/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p90/r7.claim: Another explanation is that hardship in worldly livelihood was assigned to men.
ITQAN:v3p90/r7.anchor: وقيل لأنه الله جعل الشقاء في معيشة الدنيا في جانب الرجال

ITQAN:v3p90/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p90/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p90/r8.claim: A further explanation is polite omission of the woman, in keeping with the saying that good manners conceal women.
ITQAN:v3p90/r8.anchor: وقيل إغضاء عن ذكر المرأة كما قيل من الكرم ستر الحرم

ITQAN:v3p268/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p268/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p268/r3.claim: Arabic may use a singular form instead of a dual, as in the address to Adam and his spouse ending in the singular ta sh qā.
ITQAN:v3p268/r3.anchor: العشرون الاستغناء بالإفراد عن التثنية نحو ﴿ فلا يخرجنكما من الجنة فتشقى ﴾

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r9.claim: Ibn Qutayba cites shifts in addressee, including a question to Moses and Aaron that names Moses alone, and a reference to humanity’s father Adam.
